look_here_first: Look at the leaf and climbing organ together: crossvine usually has two broad leaflets, with the third leaflet position modified into a branched tendril ending in adhesive pads.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: evergreen to semi-evergreen woody climbing vine

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: third leaflet position modified into a branched tendril

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: tendril branches end in adhesive discs/pads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaflets broad, glossy and mostly entire

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: showy orange-red to reddish/yellow trumpet-shaped flowers

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: long flattened 2-valved capsule with winged seeds

lookalikes.differences: The two-leaflet-plus-tendril architecture is the fastest way to separate crossvine from trumpet creeper.
